item.title: Cardio-Oncology Establishes Itself as a Mature Medical Specialty Across Global Healthcare - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Evolution, clinical framework, and institutional maturation of cardio-oncology as a distinct medical specialty
  • Article Title: The emerging discipline has emerged: cardio-oncology as a medical specialty
  • The emerging discipline has emerged: cardio-oncology as a medical specialty. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, 13, Article 1954059. https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1954059

본문

Advances in modern oncology have transformed many previously fatal malignancies into chronic and manageable conditions, generating an unprecedented global population of long-term cancer survivors who now confront significant treatment-related cardiovascular complications. In an analysis published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, researchers Yohannes T. Ghebre, Derek R. Shyr, and Pius S. Fasinu report that cardio-oncology has crossed the critical threshold from an emerging consultative niche into an established medical specialty. What originally originated as isolated consultations focused primarily on anthracycline-induced heart failure has expanded into a comprehensive clinical framework encompassing baseline risk stratification, multimodal surveillance, acute complication management, and lifelong survivorship care. The authors observe that cardiovascular disease now represents one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among cancer survivors, necessitating an integrated clinical discipline that protects cardiovascular function while enabling patients to receive optimal, uninterrupted cancer treatments.

The clinical imperative driving this institutional maturation is illustrated by therapeutic shifts in specific malignancies, such as Human Epidermal growth factor Receptor 2 positive breast cancer, where modern targeted regimens have dramatically improved overall survival while introducing cardiovascular toxicities that can compromise therapy, diminish quality of life, and elevate long-term mortality. Modern clinical practice can no longer focus solely on eradicating malignant disease without addressing the preservation of cardiovascular health. Oncology and cardiovascular medicine are increasingly interconnected through common traditional risk factors, including advanced age, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, obesity, tobacco exposure, chronic systemic inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction. Beyond shared lifestyle and environmental exposures, emerging biological evidence demonstrates direct crosstalk between oncologic disease processes and cardiovascular pathophysiology, indicating that malignant conditions and cardiovascular disease frequently coexist through overlapping mechanisms rather than simple clinical coincidence, creating a complex patient population requiring specialized multidisciplinary expertise.

item.title: Inhibiting Lysozyme 2 Promotes Cardiac Repair in Mice After Myocardial Infarction - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Targeting lysozyme 2 in remote endocardial zones to promote cardiac repair
  • Article Title: Targeting lysozyme 2 in remote endocardial zones promotes rapid cardiac repair after injury
  • Targeting lysozyme 2 in remote endocardial zones promotes rapid cardiac repair after injury. Cell Regeneration, 14(1), Article 42. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13619-025-00267-5

본문

A study led by Fan and colleagues, highlighted by Xiuxiu Liu and Bin Zhou in Cell Regeneration, demonstrates that targeting lysozyme 2 in remote endocardial zones promotes rapid cardiac structural repair and functional recovery in mice following myocardial infarction. While adult mammalian hearts typically lack the capacity to regenerate after injury—a major factor contributing to progressive heart failure—the researchers identified a previously unrecognized pathological mechanism operating far beyond the primary injury site.

Whereas conventional cardiac repair research has focused predominantly on cardiomyocyte proliferation directly surrounding local infarct zones, the investigation shifted attention to remote left ventricle endocardial regions. In non-regenerative hearts, the researchers identified sustained activity of lysozyme 2 (Lyz2) as a critical driver of structural damage, demonstrating that localized ischemic injury triggers detrimental biochemical events in distant cardiac tissues.

The study delineated the cellular cascade through which Lyz2 impairs cardiac healing, establishing that its persistent activity drives lysosomal degradation of the extracellular matrix. Consequently, loss of extracellular matrix integrity was found to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis near the endocardium, compounding post-injury cardiac cell loss.

To explore therapeutic potential, the investigators evaluated both the genetic deletion of Lyz2 and the pharmacological inhibition of lysosomal degradation activity in mice subjected to myocardial infarction. Both interventions successfully preserved extracellular matrix integrity, significantly reduced cardiomyocyte apoptosis in remote zones, diminished myocardial scarring, and led to measurable improvements in cardiac function.

These cellular and physiological outcomes redefine Lyz2 as a remote-injury-triggered regulator of lysosomal degradation that actively impedes tissue recovery. In probing how injury messages travel across cardiac compartments, the study highlighted inter-tissue communication and proposed ERK/STAT3 signaling as a potential molecular mediator coordinating this remote endocardial response.

item.title: Mechanical Stress Genes Reveal Two Distinct Immune Subtypes in Heart Failure - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Mechanical stimulus-related genes, diagnostic biomarkers, and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure
  • Article Title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure
  • Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, 13, Article 1953634. https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1953634

본문

A multi-omics research study combining machine learning algorithms, single-cell sequencing, and animal modeling has identified 53 mechanical stimulus-related genes altered in heart failure, establishing an 11-gene diagnostic biomarker panel and distinguishing two distinct molecular disease subtypes. Published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine by Cheng Zhang, Linna Zhao, Jiahuan Sun, Xiaodan Wang, Chuang Zhang, and Ai-Ying Li from the Hebei University of Chinese Medicine, the study investigated how mechanical stress forces correlate with immune microenvironment remodeling during the progression of cardiac dysfunction. While abnormal physical stress is recognized as a trigger for maladaptive cardiac remodeling, the systematic contribution of mechanical stimulus-related genes to heart failure diagnosis and immune modulation has remained poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, the research team analyzed bulk transcriptomic datasets alongside curated gene sets from the Molecular Signatures Database, systematically comparing gene expression profiles between heart failure specimens and healthy control tissues to identify candidate differentially expressed genes.

From the initial screening of 53 differentially expressed mechanical stimulus-related genes, the investigators implemented a multi-tiered computational strategy to isolate the most reliable diagnostic markers. Rather than relying on a single statistical approach, the team jointly applied three complementary machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE). By intersecting the feature selections across these three algorithms, the authors narrowed the 53 candidates down to 11 core diagnostic biomarkers. Using these 11 selected genes, the researchers constructed a clinical nomogram model designed for diagnostic prediction. In computational evaluations, the resulting nomogram demonstrated high predictive performance, indicating that the combined expression levels of these 11 mechanical stress genes can effectively distinguish heart failure profiles from healthy controls.

item.title: AHA 2026: Pharmacists at the Center of Cardiometabolic Care - Pharmacy Times
item.description:
요약

  • AHA 2026: Pharmacists at the Center of Cardiometabolic Care
  • - Interim CORALreef Extension data for oral PCSK9 inhibitor enlicitide showed sustained LDL-C reductions and no new safety signals over ~4200 patient-years, with adherence reinforcement critical in asymptomatic disease.
  • From survodutide titration to oral PCSK9 adherence and HF care models, AHA 2026 experts pointed to pharmacists as key to putting new data into practice.

본문

AHA 2026: Pharmacists at the Center of Cardiometabolic Care

- Survodutide’s SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT established CV safety (HR 0.89; CI crossed 1), while GI AE–driven discontinuation near 20% during escalation supports pharmacist-led, tolerability-guided titration.

- Interim CORALreef Extension data for oral PCSK9 inhibitor enlicitide showed sustained LDL-C reductions and no new safety signals over ~4200 patient-years, with adherence reinforcement critical in asymptomatic disease.

From survodutide titration to oral PCSK9 adherence and HF care models, AHA 2026 experts pointed to pharmacists as key to putting new data into practice.

When the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 convened in Chicago, Illinois, from November 6 to 9, 2026, the data spanned a new class of incretin-based therapy, longer-term results for the first oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, blood pressure effects of an oral glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, and real-world models of heart failure (HF) care. Across Pharmacy Times interviews and abstract coverage from the meeting, a common theme emerged: pharmacists are increasingly central to how new cardiometabolic therapies are titrated, monitored, and sustained.1-4

Presenters ranged from trial principal investigators, including Biykem Bozkurt, MD, PhD, of Baylor College of Medicine, and Christie Ballantyne, MD, also of Baylor College of Medicine, to pharmacist leaders such as Cody Parsons, PharmD, APh, BCCCP, of Stanford Health Care. On tolerability and dosing for a new agent, Bozkurt put it plainly: "Pharmacists are critical in identifying individual needs, tolerability, and AE profile."1-3

Investigators Share Valuable Insights on Cardiometabolic Care

A New Incretin Class Clears a Safety Bar

In the phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT trial (NCT06077864), survodutide (Zealand Pharma, Boehringer Ingelheim), an investigational once-weekly glucagon/GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, did not increase the risk of 5-point major adverse cardiovascular events versus placebo in adults with obesity or overweight and elevated cardiovascular risk (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.67-1.18). Bozkurt, the trial's principal investigator, explained that because glucagon receptor agonism may have direct effects on the cardiovascular system, the new class needed its own noninferiority trial. Because the CIs crossed 1, the results establish safety rather than benefit.1,5

item.title: Men and Women Show Distinct Acute Heart Failure Profiles but Similar Mortality - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Sex-specific clinical phenotypes and prognostic markers in acute heart failure
  • Article Title: Sex differences in clinical phenotypes and prognostic associations in acute heart failure
  • Sex differences in clinical phenotypes and prognostic associations in acute heart failure. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, 13, Article 2011890. https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.2011890

본문

Men and women hospitalized for acute heart failure present with markedly different clinical, metabolic, and renal profiles, yet they experience comparable in-hospital and post-discharge mortality rates, according to an observational study published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine. Recognizing that women remain historically under-represented in major cardiovascular trials and that established risk markers derive predominantly from male cohorts, researchers investigated whether physiological profiles and marker-based prognostic associations diverge systematically according to patient sex. The resulting analysis demonstrates that while baseline clinical characteristics differ extensively between female and male patients, statistical evidence does not support broad differences in how traditional risk factors predict post-discharge survival.

The investigation drew upon data from a prospective, single-center acute heart failure registry conducted in Heraklion, Greece, by a collaborative medical and research team representing the General Hospital of Heraklion Venizeleio-Pananio, the University General Hospital of Heraklion, the University of Crete School of Medicine, and the Foundation for Research and Technology. Investigators analyzed 530 consecutive patients admitted with acute heart failure, among whom 284 participants, or 53.6 percent, were men. Survival analyses focused on the cohort of 503 patients who were successfully discharged alive from the hospital, using Cox proportional hazards regression to model post-discharge mortality, test eight primary clinical covariates for sex interactions, and screen nineteen metabolic, inflammatory, and renal laboratory markers for sex-specific effect modification.

Clinical comparisons revealed substantial baseline demographic and phenotypic divergences between the sexes at the time of acute hospital admission. Women were also significantly more likely to exhibit heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, observed in 65.9 percent of female patients versus 35.9 percent of male patients, and had higher rates of documented frailty at 74.0 percent compared with 59.9 percent in men, alongside a higher prevalence of chronic kidney disease. Conversely, male patients were more frequently diagnosed with an ischemic etiology for their heart failure, accounting for 45.8 percent of men compared to only 15.0 percent of women, although investigators noted that coronary anatomy was left unassessed significantly more often in female patients.

Biochemical and echocardiographic evaluations similarly distinguished the two cohorts upon hospital admission. Female patients exhibited higher average circulating total cholesterol levels, measuring 139 milligrams per deciliter compared with 126 milligrams per deciliter in men, lower circulating cardiac troponin concentrations, and a higher echocardiographic E/e′ ratio within the subset of patients presenting with preserved ejection fraction.

item.title: Left Atrial Strain Aids Detection of Cardiac Amyloidosis in Heart Muscle Thickening - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Diagnostic potential and prognostic value of left atrial reservoir strain in pathological left ventricular hypertrophy
  • Article Title: Determinants of left atrial reservoir strain and diagnostic potential for cardiac amyloidosis in pathological left ventricular hypertrophy
  • Determinants of left atrial reservoir strain and diagnostic potential for cardiac amyloidosis in pathological left ventricular hypertrophy. Cardiovascular Ultrasound, 23(1), Article 4. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12947-025-00339-1

본문

Echocardiographic measurements of left atrial reservoir strain are closely linked to mechanical function at the base of the left ventricle and provide valuable diagnostic utility for identifying cardiac amyloidosis among patients presenting with pathological left ventricular hypertrophy. In an observational investigation evaluating 341 patients with abnormal left ventricular wall thickening, researchers demonstrated that mechanics in the left atrium reflect regional longitudinal shortening at the basal myocardium. This physiological coupling between the atrium and the ventricular base offers clinicians an additional noninvasive parameter when conducting etiological assessments of hypertrophic heart conditions and evaluating patient risks for subsequent heart failure complications.

Pathological left ventricular hypertrophy represents a profound form of structural remodeling that serves as a well-established risk factor for heart failure onset. Thickening of the ventricular walls arises from distinct histological changes in myocardial tissue, ranging from primary myocyte cellular hypertrophy and progressive interstitial fibrosis to the pathological extracellular deposition of misfolded protein fibrils, such as amyloid. These structural modifications impair the diastolic filling properties of the chamber, causing delayed myocardial relaxation and elevated passive stiffness. While conventional transthoracic echocardiography remains the primary noninvasive modality for estimating wall thickness and diastolic severity, patients often experience silent declines in myocardial longitudinal shortening even when their overall left ventricular ejection fraction appears preserved on routine examination.

Speckle tracking echocardiography addresses these diagnostic challenges by directly evaluating longitudinal wall mechanics across distinct myocardial segments, permitting earlier detection of subclinical systolic impairment than traditional volumetric ejection fraction metrics. In clinical cohorts with abnormal hypertrophy, a recognizable strain distribution termed the apical sparing pattern frequently points toward cardiac amyloidosis. In this distinct geometric deformation profile, longitudinal shortening at the basal myocardial segments is substantially reduced despite relative preservation of contractile strain toward the ventricular apex. Because the physical descent of the cardiac base produced by ventricular long-axis contraction serves as an essential mechanical contributor to left atrial reservoir filling, structural damage localized to basal tissue directly compromises atrial hemodynamics.

item.title: Chinese Medicine Injections Show Adjuvant Heart Failure Benefits in Network Meta-Analysis - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Comparative efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese medicine injections as adjuvant therapy for ischemic heart failure
  • Article Title: Comparative efficacy and safety of six traditional Chinese medicine injections for ischemic heart failure: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
  • Comparative efficacy and safety of six traditional Chinese medicine injections for ischemic heart failure: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, 13, Article 1969858. https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1969858

본문

A large-scale Bayesian network meta-analysis published in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine reports that incorporating specific traditional Chinese medicine injections alongside conventional medical regimens can yield measurable improvements in cardiac function and symptom control for patients diagnosed with ischemic heart failure. Heart failure represents a major clinical syndrome characterized by structural and functional cardiac abnormalities that impair ventricular systolic or diastolic performance, ultimately serving as the end stage of various cardiovascular disorders. Epidemiological assessments estimate that approximately 56 million individuals worldwide live with heart failure, including roughly 12.1 million adults in China. Because ischemic heart disease stemming from coronary atherosclerosis accounts for the vast majority of these cases, researchers sought to establish whether adjuvant intravenous Chinese herbal preparations could provide measurable physiological advantages when combined with guideline-directed treatments.

To evaluate the comparative clinical efficacy and safety of these pharmacological strategies, a research team led by Yu Shang, Penglu Wei, and Hongxu Liu from Beijing University of Chinese Medicine and the Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine systematically synthesized evidence from randomized controlled trials. Across mainland clinical centers, clinicians frequently administer traditional Chinese medicine injections as adjuncts to standard pharmaceutical regimens due to their multi-target pharmacological mechanisms, rapid onset, and high systemic bioavailability. Despite their widespread use in domestic healthcare settings, direct head-to-head clinical trials comparing different injection types have remained unavailable. Consequently, the investigators applied a Bayesian network framework across both direct and indirect comparative data to evaluate six widely prescribed preparations: Shenmai injection, Shengmai injection, Shenfu injection, Xinmailong injection, Huangqi injection, and Yiqifumai injection.

item.title: Lung Ultrasound B-Lines Accurately Gauge Heart Filling Pressures and Predict Risk - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Diagnostic performance of lung ultrasound B-lines in evaluating left ventricular filling pressure and diastolic dysfunction in heart failure
  • Article Title: Diagnostic value of lung ultrasound B-lines for evaluating left ventricular filling pressure
  • Diagnostic value of lung ultrasound B-lines for evaluating left ventricular filling pressure. Cardiovascular Ultrasound, 23(1), Article 6. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12947-025-00341-7

본문

Thoracic lung ultrasound examinations that quantify vertical artifacts known as B-lines can accurately identify elevated left ventricular filling pressure and help classify diastolic dysfunction in patients evaluated for heart failure. In a prospective clinical study conducted at Masuda Red Cross Hospital, investigators evaluated whether counting B-lines across defined thoracic scan areas could provide an objective, noninvasive alternative to conventional echocardiographic measures that frequently fail to deliver conclusive diagnostic results. The research team discovered that the quantity of detected B-lines rose progressively alongside worsening grades of left ventricular diastolic dysfunction determined through standard professional guidelines. Furthermore, direct comparison against invasive cardiac catheterization data established a statistically significant correlation between thoracic B-line counts and left ventricular pre-atrial pressures. When integrated directly into existing noninvasive diagnostic pathways as a substitute for tricuspid regurgitation peak gradient measurements, the addition of B-line counts resolved technical diagnostic hurdles and sharply improved diagnostic specificity while preserving strong clinical sensitivity across evaluated cardiac cohorts.

Heart failure triggered by impaired left ventricular diastolic function characteristically precipitates elevated left ventricular filling pressure, which subsequently causes fluid accumulation within pulmonary structures and leads to clinical congestion. Because sustained increases in filling pressure substantially amplify the broader risk of adverse cardiovascular events and patient mortality, establishing an accurate, timely assessment of left ventricular diastolic performance and internal filling pressures represents an essential requirement in ongoing clinical practice. Clinicians routinely rely upon noninvasive transthoracic echocardiography to assess diastolic impairment and detect hemodynamic congestion without requiring invasive cardiac catheterization. Diagnostic standards established jointly by the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging mandate the measurement of numerous complex echocardiographic variables to categorize diastolic function. However, in routine examinations, these standardized algorithmic assessments frequently produce indeterminate or inconclusive results because specific required anatomical and Doppler parameters cannot be clearly visualized or accurately quantified in every patient presenting with suspected or confirmed cardiac dysfunction.

item.title: Surgeons Complete Heart Transplant After Fontan Failure and Prolonged Assist Device Support - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Pediatric orthotopic heart transplantation after Fontan failure and prolonged mechanical circulatory support
  • Article Title: Orthotopic heart transplantation for Fontan failure: experience and treatment strategy—a case report
  • Orthotopic heart transplantation for Fontan failure: experience and treatment strategy—a case report. General Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery Cases, 5(1), Article 2. https://doi.org/10.1186/s44215-025-00234-1

본문

Surgeons in Japan have reported the successful completion of an orthotopic heart transplantation in a ten-year-old boy experiencing failing Fontan circulation after three years of mechanical circulatory support with a ventricular assist device. The case report, published in General Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery Cases, details the intricate surgical strategy required to address severe vascular remodeling, anatomical variations, and dense mediastinal adhesions arising from multiple prior cardiac surgeries. By establishing peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass via cervical cannulation prior to re-sternotomy, performing extensive pulmonary artery reconstruction from hilum to hilum, and utilizing deep hypothermic circulatory arrest during atrial reconstruction, the surgical team successfully overcame the substantial technical challenges associated with heart transplantation following univentricular palliation.

The patient presented with complex congenital cardiac malformations, including a large ventricular septal defect, mitral stenosis, a straddling tricuspid valve, a right-sided aortic arch with an aberrant left subclavian artery, and a retro-aortic innominate vein. At two years of age, he underwent completion of the Fontan pathway via an extracardiac total cavopulmonary connection utilizing an eighteen-millimeter expanded polytetrafluoroethylene conduit. Following this palliative procedure, the patient experienced gradual deterioration of systemic ventricular function over several years. Due to progressive heart failure and persistent inotrope dependence at seven years of age, a Berlin Heart EXCOR Pediatric ventricular assist device was implanted to serve as a bridge to heart transplantation, at which point the child was listed as a transplant candidate.

A critical contextual factor described in the clinical report is the prolonged pre-transplant waiting interval encountered in Japan relative to Western clinical centers. In Western countries, pediatric heart transplantation is typically carried out within a few months of active listing, whereas donor organ scarcity in Japan often extends waiting times considerably. For this child, approximately three years elapsed between the implantation of the ventricular assist device and donor organ availability. Prolonged mechanical circulatory support during childhood introduces unique surgical complications, including localized infections at cannula exit sites, extensive intrathoracic scarring, and the progressive exhaustion of conventional central venous access routes resulting from repeated interventions.

item.title: Framework Synthesizes Ventilator Liberation Evidence for Cardiogenic Shock and Heart Failure - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Ventilator liberation frameworks in cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure
  • Article Title: Cardiac-limited ventilator liberation in cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure: a critical care cardiology framework
  • Cardiac-limited ventilator liberation in cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure: a critical care cardiology framework. Critical Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13054-026-06379-x

본문

Respiratory support is widely utilized in patients experiencing cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure, yet disease-specific evidence guiding clinical management remains limited across multiple stages of care. In a narrative review published in Critical Care, researchers Aryan Shiari and Andrew Boshara evaluate the evidence base surrounding intubation, spontaneous breathing trials, extubation, post-extubation support, and liberation during mechanical circulatory support.

To examine these clinical challenges, the authors synthesized available cardiovascular and respiratory physiology alongside randomized trial evidence from adjacent patient populations. The review also incorporates data gathered from cardiogenic shock registries, investigations focused on weaning-induced pulmonary edema, and published literature covering mechanical circulatory support, including venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO).

A central distinction articulated in the review separates weaning-induced pulmonary edema as a specific diagnostic phenotype from cardiac-limited ventilator liberation as a broader decisional framework. Under this framework, pulmonary mechanics may appear clinically adequate, but a patient’s liberation from mechanical ventilation is primarily constrained by limited cardiovascular reserve, elevated respiratory effort, or ongoing mechanical circulatory device strategies.

Because existing evidence across these clinical areas remains largely observational, the authors emphasize that their synthesis does not provide guideline-level recommendations. Instead, the framework is structured to organize bedside assessments, delineate the boundary where empirical evidence ends and expert opinion begins, and outline future research priorities within critical care cardiology.

Subject of Research: Ventilator liberation frameworks in cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure

Article Title: Cardiac-limited ventilator liberation in cardiogenic shock and advanced heart failure: a critical care cardiology framework

item.title: ECG Patterns Identify Early Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Asymptomatic Bundle Branch Block - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Screening for subclinical left ventricular systolic dysfunction in isolated left bundle branch block using electrocardiography
  • Article Title: Relationship between electrocardiographic characteristics and subclinical left ventricular systolic dysfunction in isolated left bundle branch block patients
  • Relationship between electrocardiographic characteristics and subclinical left ventricular systolic dysfunction in isolated left bundle branch block patients. Cardiovascular Ultrasound, 23(1), Article 7. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12947-025-00342-6

본문

Standard electrocardiogram markers can identify early subclinical left ventricular systolic dysfunction in asymptomatic patients diagnosed with isolated left bundle branch block who retain a preserved ejection fraction, according to findings from a retrospective observational study conducted by researchers at the First Hospital of China Medical University. Left bundle branch block, a condition originating from abnormal electrical conduction within the His bundle or its derivative branches, manifests on surface electrocardiography as a widened QRS complex alongside characteristic morphological alterations. While the condition frequently appears alongside structural cardiovascular disorders such as ischemic or nonischemic cardiomyopathies, where it denotes an unfavorable clinical prognosis, it can also manifest in asymptomatic individuals displaying no overt structural anomalies. In this subset of patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, insidious contractile impairments may already be present and silently advancing. When subclinical systolic dysfunction remains undetected over extended periods, affected individuals face an increased likelihood of progressing toward substantial cardiac diseases and experiencing higher long-term mortality rates compared to peers whose systolic function remains preserved.

Although two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography serves as an established and highly sensitive imaging method to detect insidious systolic failure by quantifying myocardial strain, widespread clinical deployment faces notable barriers. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments, particularly those relying on speckle tracking, require extensive examination time, rely heavily on operator expertise, and demonstrate variability between different observers and across repeated readings. Consequently, detailed imaging examinations are overwhelmingly performed only after patients present with overt cardiovascular symptoms, limiting their practical utility as rapid initial screening instruments for asymptomatic populations. By comparison, standard twelve-lead electrocardiography represents a widely available, highly portable, rapid, and cost-effective modality suitable for broad community-level screening. Prior clinical research established that surface electrocardiograms can aid in screening for heart failure and forecasting adverse outcomes in symptomatic cohorts; however, the explicit ability of electrocardiographic characteristics to uncover hidden myocardial contractile deficits among individuals presenting with isolated left bundle branch block and preserved ejection fraction had not been systematically validated.

item.title: Telemedicine-based management program improves quality of life for heart failure patients - News-Medical
item.description:
요약

  • A telemedicine-based management program was well accepted among patients with heart failure and improved their quality of life and self-care, according to results presented today at ESC Digital & AI Summit 2026.
  • In total, 75% of participants were aged over 60 years and 74% were male. The vast majority (90%) of patients reported independent device use and 90% rated handling and data transmission as easy.
  • Patient satisfaction with the program was high: 94% considered telemonitoring a valuable concept and would recommend it to other patients. Almost 60% of program participants expressed interest in continuing to use telemonitoring.

본문

A telemedicine-based management program was well accepted among patients with heart failure and improved their quality of life and self-care, according to results presented today at ESC Digital & AI Summit 2026.

Patients with heart failure suffer a triad of high mortality rates, frequent rehospitalizations and reduced quality of life. Telemonitoring-based programs have emerged as promising approaches to support the continuity of care, particularly following hospital discharge when patients are at high risk of re-admission and mortality.

Study presenter, Doctor Andreas Prenner from the Styrian Hospital Corporation (KAGes), Graz, Austria, explained: "Remote telemonitoring provides a way of integrating care, bringing general practitioners together with specialist doctors and nurses to support the daily needs of the patient. Such programs can also educate patients and empower them to play an active role in their own care. We evaluated acceptance, quality of life and self-care behavior in patients discharged after an acute heart failure episode who took part in the telemedicine-supported HerzMobil Steiermark program."

The multidisciplinary, remote telemonitoring HerzMobil program was developed in Austria, with feasibility shown in a small pilot study. At the ESC Digital & AI Summit, results were presented from patients taking part in the HerzMobil Steiermark program at nine centres in the Styria region from 2019 to 2025. Patients used a simply designed app, which was linked to a weighing scale and a blood pressure and heart rate monitor for daily transmission of data. Patients were also asked to record details of whether they took their medication and how they felt each day. The data were regularly reviewed by a network of specialized nurses and physicians, who could send messages directly to the patient and arrange phone calls or in-person visits when needed.

Data were analyzed from 1,709 questionnaires collected at baseline and 1,526 after three months of follow-up.

In total, 75% of participants were aged over 60 years and 74% were male. The vast majority (90%) of patients reported independent device use and 90% rated handling and data transmission as easy.

The program demonstrated clinically relevant improvements in health status and quality of life, measured using the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ). The overall summary KCCQ score (range: 0-100) increased from 62.6 points at baseline to 76.9 points after three months in the programme. Improvements were seen across all KCCQ domains, including reductions in physical limitations and symptom burden, and better self-efficacy and quality of life.
